title: Pigeons can tell a Monet from a Picasso
topic: Trained pigeons sorted paintings by artist, then generalised to painters they had never been shown
voice_script: Pigeons can tell a Monet from a Picasso. Researchers in Tokyo trained them on paintings they had never seen, rewarding pecks at one artist and not the other. The birds learned it quickly. Then they were shown new paintings, and they still sorted them correctly. They also sorted painters they had never been trained on, putting the impressionists on one side and the cubists on the other. The pigeons were not recognizing paintings. They had learned a style.
